verses.note: The verse introduces the image of God: humanity made in God's image and likeness, with rule over the creatures as its first expression. Christian theology has read the image as reason, as royal representation, as relationship, or as a combination; the verse's own emphasis falls on representation and vocation.

Both male and female bear the image. The verse makes the image the possession of humanity as such, which the New Testament later grounds in Christ, the image of the invisible God into whose likeness believers are renewed (Colossians 1:15, 3:10).

Human life is protected because human beings bear God's image (Genesis 9:6). Jesus extended the command to anger and contempt (Matthew 5:21-22), treating it as a guard over the neighbor's worth, not only a ban on the final act.
The title ‘sons of God’ is given to those who share God's own work of reconciliation. Sonship here is shown in likeness: those who make peace resemble the God of peace.

The image of God, damaged in the fall, is restored in the image of the Son. Humanity was made in God's image (Genesis 1:27); believers are being remade in the image of Christ, who is himself the image of God (2 Corinthians 4:4, Colossians 1:15).
